text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 20 in history:
1303 - The Treaty of Paris restored Gascony to the British in the Hundred Years War.
1347 - In Rome, Cola di Rienza took the title of Tribune and assumed dictatorial powers in his drive to revive the city as the capital of Italy.

1364 - Sir Henry Percy, English rebel who led an uprising against King Henry IV, born. Better known by his nickname Harry Hotspur, Shakespeare used him as a major character in his two-part play Henry IV.
1498 - The explorer Vasco da Gama arrived at Calicut, India, to complete his voyage around Africa.
1501 - The Portuguese discovered an island in the south Atlantic on Ascension Day and named it Ascension Island.
1506 - Christopher Columbus, Italian navigator and explorer, died. His four voyages to the New World led to European exploitation and colonisation.
1537 - Hieronymous Fabricius, Italian anatomist who helped found modern embryology, born.
1759 - William Thornton, U.S. architect responsible for the original design of Washington's Capitol building, born.
1774 - Britain passed the Quebec Act, extending its boundaries northwards to Hudson's Bay land and as far south as the junction of the Ohio and Mississippi rivers.
1799 - Honore de Balzac, French novelist notably of "The Human Comedy", born.
1818 - William George Fargo, who along with Henry Wells founded the Wells-Fargo company, born.
1834 - Marie Joseph Gilbert de Motier, French soldier and statesman known as the Marquis de Lafayette, died. He fought alongside the American colonists against the British in the American Revolution.
1867 - In London, Queen Victoria laid the foundation stone of the Royal Albert Hall.
1881 - Wladyslaw Sikorski, Polish General and statesman who led the Free Polish forces during World War Two, born.
1902 - Cuba was handed over to a republican government and the last U.S. troops left.
1904 - Margery Allingham, English novelist who created the amateur detective Albert Campion, born.
1908 - James Stewart, American actor, born. He won an Oscar for "The Philadelphia Story" in 1940 and was honoured with a special award in 1985.

1915 - Moshe Dayan, Israeli military commander and statesman, born. He led Israeli forces during the invasion of Sinai in 1956 and the Six-Day War of 1967 and held defence and foreign affairs cabinet posts.
1922 - The P&O liner Egypt sank off Ushant after colliding in fog with the French steamship Seine, with the loss of 90 lives. The ship was also carrying one million sterling worth of gold and silver.
1923 - British Prime Minister Bonar Law resigned due to ill health and was replaced by Stanley Baldwin.
1927 - The Treaty of Jeddah was signed between Great Britain and King Ibn Saud, recognising the independence of Saudi Arabia.
1939 - Pan American Airways began the first regular transatlantic airmail service across the North Atlantic.
1941 - The Mediterranean island of Crete was invaded by German troops.
1944 - Joe Cocker, English singer and drummer whose biggest hit was "With A Little Help From My Friends", born as John Robert Cocker.
1945 - U.S. pop singer Cher was born as Cherilyn La Pierre. Had a long partnership with Sonny Bono as Sonny and Cher.
1956 - The first hydrogen bomb to be dropped from the air was exploded by the Americans over the Bikini Atoll in the Pacific.
1972 - Referendum in Cameroon approved change of country from federation into a unitary state.
1980 - The Canadian province of Quebec voted against a proposal to negotiate independence from Canada.
1983 - In one of the worst terrorist attacks in South Africa, about 20 people died in a car bomb explosion outside the Air Force headquarters in Pretoria.
1989 - Martial law was imposed in Peking after student-led protests drew millions of people onto the streets.
1991 - The Soviet parliament approved in principle a law which would allow citizens to travel aboard freely.
1993 - The British parliament finally passed a bill aimed at ratifying the Maastricht treaty, after six months of feuding.
1995 - A riot began at the Whitehead detention camp in Hong Kong by refugees about to be forcably repatriated to Vietnam.
1996 - Iraq, whose economy had been devastated by nearly six years of sanctions, accepted a tough U.N. plan to sell limited quantities of oil in order to buy food and medicine.
